business.body: Lohia Corp Limited manufactures machinery and equipment for technical textiles, focused on solutions for producing polypropylene (PP) and high-density polyethylene (HDPE) woven fabric and sacks ("Raffia"), and provides end-to-end 'concept to commissioning' solutions across the woven fabric production lifecycle. Its machines are sold to producers of woven fabric used in packaging (cement, fertilizer, chemicals, polymer, food grain, minerals) and non-packaging applications, supplied to around 100 countries through an exclusive global sales network. business_ops.seasonality: The production and sale of technical textiles and consequently sales volumes may be affected by general economic or industry conditions, including seasonal trends in the agriculture sector, recessionary trends in the global and domestic economies and volatility in construction. The cyclical nature of the agriculture and construction industries, both globally and in India, impacts the demand for packaging of bulk commodities, which in turn affects demand for machinery and equipment for manufacturing technical textiles. In particular, the agricultural sector is inherently seasonal and is further impacted by factors including agricultural commodity prices, costs of fertilizers and adverse weather conditions. Similarly, the construction sector is prone to seasonality owing to factors such as the inconsistent real estate market and economic downturns that cease construction activity. No seasonality figures or quarterly split for the issuer's own revenue are disclosed in the routed text.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration capabilities reduce dependence on external supply of parts and components for machine manufacturing and support services and enable maintenance of quality control. The Company designs and manufactures inverters, customized machine controllers and motors along with other products for its circular weaving machine and winders, and operates its own surface mount technology manufacturing line for printed circuit board assembly and testing, so inverters, controllers and motors are made in-house for use either as original parts or spare parts. It has an in-house sheet metal fabrication shop catering to all sheet metal part requirements, 100 computer numerical control (CNC) machines that manufacture parts required in its machines, and a 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) from a global internal precision-equipment supplier for adherence to specifications. Electrical parts like inverters and printed circuit boards are also produced in-house using imported electric parts manufacturing equipment, aided by electrical assembly shops at each manufacturing facility where electrical panels are assembled. Other manufacturing steps are integrated through plating shops, moulding shops, assembly and testing shops and paint shops located within the manufacturing facilities, minimising dependence on external service providers. On the inbound side, raw materials, parts and components are sourced from suppliers on a purchase order basis, usually valid for one and two years, without formal long-term agreements; key externally sourced components include extrusion die, pump and screw, gear-box, bearings, electric motors and drives, and certain key components such as electrical motors, sensors, PLC systems, invertors and gear boxes are procured from limited suppliers in India, Europe, USA, China and Japan. Forward reach is through an exclusive global sales network: four sales offices in India (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Kolkata, New Delhi) plus a corporate office, five international offices (Brazil, Russia, Thailand, UAE, USA), warehouses in India, UAE and USA, stockists in eight countries, 17 exclusive sales agents, and service engineers stationed in 12 cities in India and in 12 countries overseas.

overview.business_model: The Company manufactures and sells machinery and equipment used to make woven plastic (Raffia) fabric and sacks - tape extrusion lines, winders, circular looms, coating and lamination lines, printing machines, conversion machines, multifilament yarn machines, twister winders, monofilament extrusion lines and recycling machines - to a global customer base through an extensive global sales and distribution network.

genesis.founding_story: The Company was incorporated as "Kanpur Packaging Machines Limited", a company limited by shares, under the Companies Act, pursuant to a certificate of incorporation dated June 5, 2023 issued by the Registrar of Companies, Central Registration Center. The Company had no operations since its incorporation on June 5, 2023 and prior to the Scheme being effective.

compliance_legal.detail: Under current Indian tax laws, unless specifically exempted, capital gains arising from the sale of equity shares in an Indian company are generally taxable in India, and a securities transaction tax is levied on equity shares sold on an Indian stock exchange. compliance_legal.evidence: "Any capital gains exceeding ₹125,000, realized on the sale of listed equity shares on a recognised stock exchange, held for more than 12 months may be subject to long-term capital gains tax in India at the rate of 12.5% (plus applicable surcharge and cess)." "any gain realized on the sale of our Equity Shares held for a period of 12 months or less immediately preceding the date of transfer, will be subject to short-term capital gains tax in India at the rate of 20% (plus applicable surcharge and cess)"
compliance_legal.title: RF 72: Investors may be subject to Indian taxes arising out of capital gains on the sale of the Equity Shares

compliance_legal.detail: Transfers of shares between non-residents and residents are freely permitted subject to compliance with sectoral norms and other restrictions if they comply with the pricing guidelines and reporting requirements specified by the RBI; otherwise prior regulatory approval is required. Shareholders converting Rupee proceeds into foreign currency and repatriating require a no-objection or tax clearance certificate from the Indian income tax authorities. Under Press Note No. 3 (2020 Series), all investments under the foreign direct investment route by entities of a country which shares a land border with India, or where the beneficial owner is situated in or is a citizen of any such country, can only be made through the Government approval route. Neither the foreign direct investment policy nor the FEMA Rules provide a definition of the term "beneficial owner".
compliance_legal.evidence: "pursuant to the Press Note No. 3 (2020 Series), dated April 17, 2020, issued by the DPIIT"; "as prescribed in the Consolidated FDI Policy dated October 15, 2020 and the FEMA Rules"; "Furthermore, on April 22, 2020, the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, has also made similar amendment to the FEMA Rules."
compliance_legal.title: RF 75: Investment restrictions on foreign investors under Indian law

compliance_legal.detail: Under the Companies Act, a company having share capital and incorporated in India must offer holders of equity shares pre-emptive rights to subscribe and pay for a proportionate number of equity shares before the issuance of any new equity shares, unless waived by a special resolution. If the laws of the investor's jurisdiction do not permit exercise of pre-emptive rights without the Company filing an offering document or registration statement, the investor will be unable to exercise such rights unless such a filing is made; if the Company elects not to file, new securities may be issued to a custodian who may sell them for the investor's benefit.
compliance_legal.evidence: "to the extent that the investors are unable to exercise pre-emption rights granted in respect of the Equity Shares held by them, their proportional interest in us would be reduced"
compliance_legal.title: RF 82: Holders of Equity Shares may be restricted in their ability to exercise pre-emptive rights under Indian law

compliance_legal.detail: There are provisions in Indian law that may delay, deter or prevent a future takeover or change in control. Under the Takeover Regulations, an acquirer is any person who directly or indirectly acquires or agrees to acquire shares or voting rights or control over a company, individually or acting in concert with others. Even if a potential takeover would result in a purchase of Equity Shares at a premium to market price, such a takeover may not be attempted or consummated because of the Takeover Regulations.
compliance_legal.evidence: "these provisions may also discourage a third party from attempting to take control of our Company subsequent to completion of the Offer"
compliance_legal.title: RF 83: A third party could be prevented from acquiring control post-Offer because of anti-takeover provisions under Indian law

compliance_legal.detail: The Articles of Association, composition of the Board, Indian laws governing corporate affairs, the validity of corporate procedures, directors' fiduciary duties, responsibilities and liabilities, and shareholders' rights may differ from those applying to a company in another jurisdiction, and shareholders' rights under Indian law may not be as extensive as under the laws of other countries.

internal_operational.detail: Operations depend on supply chain management of raw materials, parts and components made to drawings and standard bought-out parts. Key externally sourced components are extrusion die, pump and screw, gear-box, bearings, electric motors and drives. Raw materials are sourced on a purchase order basis (usually valid for one and two years) with no formal long-term supplier agreements; some purchase orders require the Company to obtain insurance on materials supplied, bear freight costs and make 100% upfront payments prior to shipment. The Company cannot assure it will be able to pass on cost increases to customers.
internal_operational.evidence: Cost of materials consumed Fiscal 2025 (Consolidated): 6,582.74 (47.81% of revenue from operations; 53.78% of total expenses). Purchases of stock-in-trade 996.16 (7.23%; 8.14%). Total 7,663.80 (55.66%; 62.61%). Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 total 6,697.16 (57.44%; 59.06%); Fiscal 2023 total 11,776.15 (63.75%; 66.47%). "the terms of some of our purchase orders require us to obtain insurance on the materials supplied to us, bear freight costs and make 100% upfront payments prior to shipment"
internal_operational.title: RF 1: Increases, fluctuations or shortages in prices/supply of primary raw materials

internal_operational.detail: Machines have multiple parts and components sourced indigenously as well as imported. Laws governing import of raw materials may become more stringent, and adverse changes in indirect taxes, import duties, tariffs and currency exchange rate may affect the ability to source, or increase the cost of sourcing, from overseas suppliers, with no assurance that alternative or domestic suppliers can be found in a timely manner or at all.
internal_operational.evidence: Expenditure on consumption of imported raw material: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 1,137.12 (14.84% of raw material costs); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 1,010.61 (15.09%); Fiscal 2023 1,825.39 (15.50%). Top 5 import jurisdictions Fiscal 2025: Switzerland 183.93 (16.18%), USA 152.46 (13.41%), Singapore 142.36 (12.52%), Germany 107.22 (9.43%), China 101.11 (8.89%).
internal_operational.title: RF 2: Significant portion of raw materials, parts and components sourced from overseas suppliers

internal_operational.detail: The Company owns and operates six machine manufacturing facilities, with four in India and one each in USA and Italy, along with one live experience centre in India. Two Indian facilities are in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh (with the live experience centre, where flexible intermediate bulk containers are manufactured) and two in Bengaluru, Karnataka; the USA facility is in Burlington, North Carolina and the Italy facility in Como. Warehouses are in India, UAE and USA. Almost all revenue is generated from these facilities, which are subject to operating risks including political instability, strikes and lock-outs, regulatory compliance, scheduled downtimes, equipment breakdown, industrial accidents, power or water disruption, severe weather, natural disasters and outbreak of infectious diseases.
internal_operational.evidence: "We own and operate six machine manufacturing facilities, with four in India and one each in USA and Italy, along with one live experience centre in India." "While there have been no such instances in the last three Fiscals that had a material impact on our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows"
internal_operational.title: RF 4: Dependence on continued operations of manufacturing facilities; slowdown, shutdown or disruption

internal_operational.detail: Capacity utilization is affected by the capital goods procurement plan of customers, which depends on business cyclicality and seasonality of end-user industries, although the business itself is not inherently seasonal. Investments have been made for modernisation of manufacturing capacities and further investments are being undertaken to optimise existing capacity; in case of oversupply in the industry or lack of demand, expanded capacity may not be utilised efficiently. Leased warehouses and sales offices in different jurisdictions are similarly subject to under-utilization risk.
internal_operational.evidence: "While there have been no such instances in the last three Fiscals which had a material impact on our business, results of operations and financial condition, changes in demand could reduce our ability to estimate accurately future customer requirements"
internal_operational.title: RF 11: Under-utilization of manufacturing capacity and inability to effectively utilize infrastructure

internal_operational.detail: Capacity information is based on assumptions and estimates of management taken into account by the chartered engineer in calculation and verification of capacity, including assembling capacities of different machines, availability of covered surface area, capacity of handling equipment, and adjustment for a wide range of actual processes and batch sizes. Manufacturing facilities at different plants are common for products manufactured in those plants, so installed capacity for different products is interchangeable to a large extent. Installed capacity disclosed may not be comparable with the capacity registered with the Secretariat for Industrial Assistance, Ministry of Commerce & Industry, and actual production levels and utilization rates may differ significantly.
internal_operational.evidence: "Actual production levels and utilization rates may differ significantly from the estimated production capacities or historical estimated capacity utilization information of our facilities."
internal_operational.title: RF 12: Production capacity and historical capacity utilization information is based on assumptions and estimates

internal_operational.detail: The Company faces inherent risk of exposure to product defects, quality complaints and liability claims. Warranty for manufacturing defects is typically provided for 12 months from the date of commissioning or 15 months from the date of shipment of machines, whichever is earlier, over components other than electrical/electronic items. Insurance for product liability is typically not available due to the nature of the sector. For certain exported products, performance bank guarantees may be required as a percentage of the value of machines. The long useful life of some products makes it possible that latent defects might not appear for several years.
internal_operational.evidence: Warranty claims made against our products in the ordinary course of our business: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 69.39 (0.50% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 87.02 (0.75%); Fiscal 2023 111.96 (0.61%). Provision for warranties: 89.63 (0.65%); 80.00 (0.69%); 80.00 (0.43%). "warranty for manufacturing defects is typically provided for 12 months from the date of commissioning or 15 months from the date of shipment of machines, whichever is earlier"
internal_operational.title: RF 13: Customer quality requirements, product defects, recalls, warranty and product liability claims

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing processes can be dangerous to employees and an accident or death may occur at any facility, potentially resulting in loss of life or injury, destruction of property or equipment, environmental damage, manufacturing or delivery delays, suspension of operations and imposition of liabilities. Operations involve handling hazardous materials such as chromium for chromium plating of parts/components. Hazards identified include explosions, fires, mechanical failures and other operational problems, inclement weather and natural disasters, and other environmental risks.
internal_operational.evidence: "Our operations involve handling hazardous materials such as chromium for chromium plating of parts/ components, which can cause accidents resulting in serious injuries or death of employees or other persons, if improperly handled"
internal_operational.title: RF 15: Dangerous manufacturing and assembly activities; hazardous materials; disruption at facilities

internal_operational.detail: Success depends on availability of labour and maintaining a good relationship with the workforce, and on the ability to attract, hire, train and retain skilled workers. India has stringent labour legislation including detailed procedures for establishment of unions, dispute resolution and employee removal, and financial obligations upon retrenchment. The Company trains individuals at its manufacturing technology training centre in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. As of the date of the DRHP the Company is party to a collective bargaining arrangement providing for periodic increases in certain allowances. Minimum wage laws may be amended leading to upward revisions.
internal_operational.evidence: "As of May 31, 2025, our Company had 1,736 permanent employees on our payroll and 864 contract labourers." Employee benefits expense: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 1,800.46 (13.08% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 1,836.22 (15.75%); Fiscal 2023 1,908.62 (10.33%). "we have service engineers stationed in 12 cities in India, as well as in 12 countries overseas"
internal_operational.title: RF 19: Manpower-intensive business; work stoppages, wage demands and skilled personnel availability

internal_operational.detail: Independent contractors are appointed who in turn engage on-site contract labour for ancillary operations including loading/unloading works and housekeeping activities. Although labourers are not engaged directly, the Company may be held responsible for wage payments in the event of default by independent contractors. All contract labourers engaged at the facilities are assured minimum wages fixed by the state government from time to time; any requirement to offer permanent employment or upward wage revision may increase costs.
internal_operational.evidence: "As of March 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, we engaged 873, 735 and 994 contract labourers, respectively, as part of our operations. Such contract labourers amounted to 33.38%, 29.85% and 31.92%, respectively, of our total employees, as of such dates."
internal_operational.title: RF 20: Engagement of contract labour and liability for wages on contractor default

internal_operational.detail: The Company supplies parts and accessories to global manufacturers of woven raffia and must maintain a supply of spare parts and accessories to cater to customer requirements as they arise. Customer requirements for spare parts cannot be accurately anticipated before requests are made, and failure to maintain adequate inventory, particularly in different locations, may prevent swift and efficient fulfilment.
internal_operational.evidence: Revenue from spare parts for woven raffia machines: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 1,737.81 (12.62% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 1,393.57 (11.95%); Fiscal 2023 1,511.83 (8.19%).
internal_operational.title: RF 21: Failure to provide adequate spare parts and services for machinery

internal_operational.detail: Insurance coverage maintained includes property, stock and money for warehouses, transit insurance, product liability insurance, marine insurance for shipments, group personal accident policies covering permanent and contractual employees, group mediclaim policies, all-risk insurance for portable equipment, burglary, standard fire and special perils insurance for manufacturing facilities and other premises, and export-credit multi-buyer insurance policies covering specified jurisdictions. Not every risk may have been identified or insured against, and renewals may not be granted in a timely manner, at acceptable cost or at all.
internal_operational.evidence: Insurance coverage (₹ million) as of March 31, 2025 Consolidated 12,460.06; net value of assets 7,356.31; percentage of insurance coverage to net value of assets 169.38%. Demerged Business: 12,816.81 / 7,284.03 / 175.96%; 12,802.29 / 8,215.38 / 155.83%. Restated Standalone as of March 31, 2024: 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00% ("We did not avail any insurance coverage in the absence of any insurable asset during the period.")
internal_operational.title: RF 30: Insurance coverage may not be adequate to protect against all potential losses

internal_operational.detail: Quantities manufactured for sale are determined on the basis of orders received and management estimates based on historic trends and demand data and forecasts provided by the marketing and sales network. Inaccurate estimation could result in excess inventory levels or unavailability of products during increased demand. Excess inventory of parts and components may result in inventory write-downs or write-offs or sale of excess inventory at discounted prices.
internal_operational.evidence: Inventories (₹ million): as of March 31, 2025 Consolidated 2,962.12; Demerged Business 2,951.41 and 3,746.35. Inventory turnover ratio (times): 2.59; 2.27; 3.14.
internal_operational.title: RF 32: Inability to accurately forecast customer demand and maintain optimum inventory levels

internal_operational.detail: Inventory primarily consists of materials, parts and components used in manufacturing operations, and work-in-process or machines under assembling stage. Materials, manufacturing processes and finished products are susceptible to damage if not appropriately stored, handled and processed. If damage is detected during quality checks, manufacturing activities may be suspended and capacity utilization lowered.
internal_operational.evidence: "In Fiscal 2025, there was a write-down in the value of inventory amounting to ₹ 143.77 million on account of provision for slow and non-moving inventory."
internal_operational.title: RF 33: Improper storage, processing and handling of materials and products causing inventory damage

internal_operational.detail: As a technology-driven manufacturing company, the Company faces cyber threats, threats to the physical security of facilities and employees, terrorist acts, and potential business disruptions associated with information technology failures, natural disasters or public health crises. The Company must rely on safeguards put in place by customers, suppliers, joint venture partners and acquired entities, which have varying levels of cyber security expertise. Costs related to such threats may not be fully insured or indemnified.
internal_operational.evidence: "While we have not experienced any cyber-attacks or security threats in the last three Fiscals which had a material impact on our business, results of operations and financial condition"
internal_operational.title: RF 35: Cyber or other security threats and disruptions

internal_operational.detail: The Company is dependent on the continued contributions of its chairman and managing director, Raj Kumar Lohia, its whole-time director and chief operating officer, Gaurav Lohia, and its Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and members of Senior Management. Competition for qualified personnel with relevant industry expertise in India is intense, and as some key personnel approach retirement age, succession plans need to be in place and implemented.
internal_operational.evidence: "As of May 31, 2025, our Company had 1,736 permanent employees." Attrition table – Number of permanent employees at the beginning: 1,727; 2,120; 2,189. Attrition rate of permanent employees: 11.39%; 22.83%; 12.94%. "The Scheme was effective from May 1, 2024. The number of employees prior to such period refers to the employees of the Demerged Company."
internal_operational.title: RF 38: Dependence on key personnel including Promoters, Directors, KMP and Senior Management

internal_operational.detail: The Company relies on third parties for supply of raw materials, stock-in-trade, components, contract labour and power, as well as for processes and services at manufacturing, assembly, warehousing and office premises including waste management and facility management, and for licensing of certain technologies. An in-house vendor rating process is used but does not entirely eliminate the risk of unreliable vendors. Third-party transporters are used for transporting personnel to manufacturing units, supply of raw materials and delivery of products.
internal_operational.evidence: Freight and forwarding expenses: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 330.18 (2.40% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 208.72 (1.79%); Fiscal 2023 430.81 (2.33%).
internal_operational.title: RF 39: Reliance on third parties including raw material suppliers, transporters and logistics/warehouse providers

internal_operational.detail: Timely and satisfactory execution of contractual commitments depends on numerous factors including the ability to develop necessary technologies directly or through third parties. Failure to deliver products and services in a timely manner or at all, or any fault in contract execution including as a result of delays or breaches by suppliers, may lead to higher costs or penalties or the calling of performance bonds.
internal_operational.evidence: "While we have not experienced any such instances in the last three Fiscals which had a material impact on our business, results of operations and financial condition, there can be no assurance that we would not face any situations in the future"
internal_operational.title: RF 41: Breaches of contractual commitments

internal_operational.detail: Effective information and reporting systems are critical to operations. The Company is implementing certain software and reporting initiatives and upgrading its enterprise resource planning system, with no assurance that this will be completed successfully, that the reporting systems are adequate, that the new information technology system will not become quickly out-dated, or that employees will be adequately trained to operate or comply with such systems.
internal_operational.evidence: "We are implementing certain software and reporting initiatives, and upgrading our enterprise resource planning system, but we cannot assure you that this will be completed successfully."
internal_operational.title: RF 42: Information and reporting systems require monitoring, periodic checks and upgrades

internal_operational.detail: Most electricity requirements for manufacturing facilities are sourced from state electricity boards. If electricity is not available, plants may need to be shut down until adequate supply is restored. Stand-by captive generator sets and UPS systems are maintained but may not be adequate to support all operations, and increases in per unit cost of electricity may not be passable to customers.
internal_operational.evidence: Power and fuel: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 214.02 (1.55% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 218.53 (1.87%); Fiscal 2023 299.83 (1.62%).
internal_operational.title: RF 43: Dependence on adequate and uninterrupted supplies of electricity, water and fuel

internal_operational.detail: Operations may be subject to incidents of theft or damage to inventory, and the business may encounter inventory loss on account of employee theft, vendor fraud and general administrative error. Losses due to theft, fire, breakage or damage caused by other casualties could also adversely affect results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
internal_operational.evidence: "While we have not experienced any such instance in the last three Fiscals which had a material impact on our business, results of operations and financial condition"
internal_operational.title: RF 54: Fraud, theft, employee negligence or similar incidents

internal_operational.detail: Natural disasters such as typhoons, flooding and earthquakes, epidemics and pandemics such as COVID-19, and man-made disasters including acts of war and terrorist attacks may lead to economic instability in India or globally. The DRHP notes that relations between India and Pakistan continue to be fragile on the issues of terrorism, armaments and Kashmir, and that there have been continuing border disputes between India and China. Countries in Asia including India are susceptible to contagious diseases, with confirmed cases of the highly pathogenic H7N9, H5N1 and H1N1 strains of influenza in birds and swine.
internal_operational.evidence: "While we have not experienced any major disruptions or shutdowns as a result of natural or man-made disasters in the last three Fiscals which had a material impact on our business, results of operations and financial condition"
internal_operational.title: RF 61: Natural or man-made disasters, fires, epidemics, pandemics, acts of war, terrorist attacks and civil unrest

strategy_growth.detail: The Company is among the leading global manufacturers of machinery and equipment for technical textiles by revenue in 2024, with a strong focus on solutions for producing PP and HDPE woven fabric and sacks. A significant portion of revenue from operations is derived from manufacture and supply of machines for woven fabric and sacks. Demand depends on end-use products with packaging and non-packaging applications such as agriculture, horticulture, fisheries and forestry textiles, architectural and constructional textiles, clothing textiles and geotextiles. The agriculture, textiles and construction industries are cyclical and the agricultural sector is inherently seasonal. Changes in government policies, such as amendments to the Jute Packaging Material (Compulsory Use in Packaging Commodities) Act, 1987, may affect demand.
strategy_growth.evidence: "In 2024, we ranked among the top global players by revenue, with a 15.4% share of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value." Revenue from woven raffia machines: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 12,017.05 (87.28% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 9,989.17 (85.68%); Fiscal 2023 16,753.77 (90.71%). "For instance, in December 2023 and October 2024, the Ministry of Textiles, GoI ordered at least 20% of the total produced sugar to be mandatorily packaged in jute-based material."
strategy_growth.title: RF 3: Heavy dependence on the performance of the woven raffia machines market and its end-use industries

strategy_growth.detail: The global market faces environmental regulations and anti-plastic sentiment, high capital costs for advanced machinery, competition from alternative materials such as biodegradable, paper-based and jute-based packaging, raw material and component price volatility, and skilled labour shortages for machine operation. Within India, specific threats include stringent environmental regulations, rising competition from low-cost importers from China and other Asian suppliers, technology obsolescence and a modernization gap, volatility in raw material costs given reliance on petroleum-based polymers such as polypropylene, and shortage of skilled workforce for digital transition.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Despite being reusable, woven bags are still grouped under broader plastic ban or negative perceptions in many regions." "Indian machinery manufacturers have started facing competition from Chinese and other Asian suppliers offering cheaper machines."
strategy_growth.title: RF 5: Challenges facing the Indian and global woven raffia machines market

strategy_growth.detail: The Company faces significant competition from other woven raffia machine manufacturers. Key players in the global market include Starlinger & Co. GmbH, Yongming Machinery, Hengli Machinery, Tianfeng Plastic Machinery, Polystar and JP Extrusiontech. Sales and business face risks relating to rapid technological change, development of new machinery and their rapid obsolescence, evolving industry standards and significant price erosion or depreciation over the life of the machinery. Competition is primarily on product functionality, quality and reliability; design and technical skill; research and development; production capabilities; ability to meet customers' order requirements and delivery schedules; customer relationships and after-sales services; and product price.
strategy_growth.evidence: "We are a market leader in the domestic woven Raffia machines market, with a dominant market share of 40.7% by value, in Fiscal 2025."
strategy_growth.title: RF 8: Significant competitive pressures in the industry

strategy_growth.detail: The Company derives a portion of its revenues from operations outside India and has manufacturing operations across India, USA and Italy, sales offices and international offices in India, Brazil, Russia, Thailand and UAE, and warehouses in India, UAE and USA. International operations are subject to efforts to introduce or expand tariffs, changes in foreign laws and policies, demand from customers located outside India, pricing pressures and competition, social, economic, political and geopolitical conditions, compliance with local laws, distance, language and cultural differences, imposition of international sanctions, and fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates. The Company also benefits from export incentives such as duty drawbacks, the Remission of Duties and Taxes on Export Products scheme and the Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme.
strategy_growth.evidence: Revenue from operations (overseas): Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 8,010.54 (58.18%); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 5,770.47 (49.50%); Fiscal 2023 6,614.17 (35.81%). Revenues from sales outside India (top 5 countries): 2,476.14 (17.98%); 1,927.99 (16.54%); 3,193.83 (17.29%). Top 5 export jurisdictions Fiscal 2025: Egypt 603.80 (4.39%), Iraq 579.31 (4.21%), USA 549.82 (3.99%), Sri Lanka 387.59 (2.82%), Indonesia 355.62 (2.58%). "For instance, the US has imposed 25% tariffs on Indian imports, which may affect our sales in the US". "In Fiscal 2025, such export incentives amounted to ₹ 193.88 million, as per the Restated Financial Information. In Fiscals 2024 and 2023, such export incentives amounted to ₹ 155.29 million and ₹ 186.77 million, respectively".
strategy_growth.title: RF 10: Risks associated with export sales and international operations, including tariffs and anti-outsourcing legislation

strategy_growth.detail: As a technology and innovation driven company with a focus on R&D, the Company possesses technical knowledge built up through its own experiences and investment in in-house R&D capabilities. Future success may depend in part on the ability to respond to technological advances and emerging standards on a cost-effective and timely basis. Development and commercialization of new products is complex, time-consuming and costly, and rapid and frequent technology and market demand changes can render existing technologies and equipment obsolete, requiring substantial new capital expenditures or write-down of assets.
strategy_growth.evidence: "As at May 31, 2025, we had 234 on-roll employees engaged in R&D activities, representing 13.48% of our total on-roll manpower." Expenditure on R&D: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 371.13 (2.70% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 367.97 (3.16%); Fiscal 2023 286.94 (1.55%).
strategy_growth.title: RF 14: Failure to maintain or improve product offerings and technology infrastructure

strategy_growth.detail: Order book means the value of the outstanding order book as of the respective dates, calculated as the total value of purchase orders and commitments received from customers during the financial year (excluding cancelled purchase orders and commitments), net of the sale of finished goods during the same period, as increased by the outstanding purchase orders and commitments as at the previous reporting date. Order book information is not audited and only indicates future revenue, which may not be actualised. Counterparties may refuse to grant extensions, seek liquidated damages or terminate contracts.
strategy_growth.evidence: "As of March 31, 2025, our order book stood at ₹ 8,284.57 million and as of March 31, 2024 and March 31, 2023, the Demerged Company’s order book stood at ₹ 7,692.40 million and ₹ 8,747.62 million, respectively."
strategy_growth.title: RF 17: Orders in the order book may be delayed, truncated, modified or cancelled and may not translate into confirmed orders

strategy_growth.detail: The Scheme enabled growth of operations since it became effective in May 2024 (from April 1, 2024 onwards). Growth may not be sustained due to a decline in demand for machines for manufacturing woven fabric/sacks, increased price competition, lack of availability of raw materials, lack of management availability or a general slowdown in the economy. The growth strategy involves increasing market share, strengthening position in the conversions and processing machineries segment in India, improving operational efficiencies through process improvements, and augmenting scale through selective strategic acquisitions and technical alliances, which will place significant demands on management and on financial, accounting and operating systems.
strategy_growth.evidence: "in Fiscal 2025, our revenue from operations stood at ₹ 13,768.72 million while our EBITDA (Calculated as profit/(loss) for the year/ period add finance cost, depreciation and amortisation expenses, and total tax expenses) was ₹ 2,286.02 million". "revenue from operations decreased from ₹ 18,470.09 million in Fiscal 2023 to ₹ 11,658.08 million in Fiscal 2024, primarily on account of factors such as (i) decrease in the number of units produced, (ii) change in product mix, (iii) decline in sale of products to customers in Africa, Asia Pacific (excluding India and China), Europe and MENA."
strategy_growth.title: RF 18: Past performance may not be indicative of future growth; inability to sustain or manage growth or implement strategies

strategy_growth.detail: The Company routinely conducts discussions, evaluates targets and enters into agreements regarding possible joint ventures, equity investments and divestitures. Past transactions include the Demerged Company's acquisition of the business and assets of Leesona Corp. in the United States in 2019, acquisition of a lamination/coating machines business for woven fabric of a company in Bengaluru and incorporation of Sundarlam Industries Private Limited in 2021, and in 2024 the acquisition through Leesona Corp. of the business of a supplier of extruder equipment and related systems in the United States and the shareholders' agreement with OMGM SAS to form Omgm Extrusiontechnik S.R.L. Growth through acquisitions may be constrained by rights held by collaborators, joint venture partners or minority shareholders, including the OMGM shareholders' agreement rights and the SIPL shareholders' agreement non-compete arrangement.
strategy_growth.evidence: "the shareholders’ agreement entered into in respect of our Subsidiary, OMGM, grants certain rights to another party (40% quota-holder of OMGM), including the right to nominate two out of the five directors on the board (including the managing director)". "under the shareholders agreement dated October 22, 2021 (as amended) ("SIPL SHA") between Raj Kumar Lohia (one of our individual promoters) and Sundaram S"; "Sundaram S (the 20% minority shareholder of SIPL) is prohibited from competing, directly, or indirectly, with the business of SIPL for the later of (a) 10 years from the execution of the SIPL SHA, plus an additional cooling off period of two years".
strategy_growth.title: RF 28: Failure to manage mergers, acquisitions, divestitures and other transactions successfully

strategy_growth.detail: The ability to differentiate the brand and products from competitors through promotional, marketing and advertising initiatives is an important factor in attracting customers. The Company, its suppliers, customers or their affiliates may be subject to negative publicity in relation to issues such as anti-corruption, safety and environmental protection, which even if later proven false or misleading could lead to a temporary or prolonged negative perception of the brand. Maintaining and enhancing brand image may require significant expenditures and investments in research and development, advertising and marketing, and employee development and training.
strategy_growth.evidence: Advertisement and marketing expenses: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 74.16 (0.54% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 125.16 (1.07%); Fiscal 2023 303.46 (1.64%).
strategy_growth.title: RF 36: Inability to maintain and enhance the brand

strategy_growth.detail: Pursuing cost-cutting measures while maintaining rigorous quality standards may lead to an erosion of margins. Estimating amounts of price reductions is subject to risk and uncertainties as any price reduction is the result of negotiations and other factors. Customers also negotiate for larger discounts in price as the volume of their orders increases. To maintain profit margins the Company seeks price reductions from suppliers, improved production processes to increase manufacturing efficiency and streamlined product designs to reduce costs.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Accordingly, machinery manufacturing companies like us must be able to reduce their operating costs in order to maintain profitability."
strategy_growth.title: RF 40: Pricing pressure from customers may affect margins, profitability and ability to increase prices

strategy_growth.detail: As part of its growth strategies the Company intends to expand new lines of business such as recycling machines for plastic waste, and to develop new machines to enter the market for post-consumer recycling for non-food grades. Key initiatives include the recycling machine, the 'ReclaMax' shredder for Raffia waste, with a pipeline including the 'ReclaPro' cutter-compactor for film and post-consumer recycling, modular washing systems with wastewater treatment and AI-driven sorting technologies. New lines of business may not be successful or enjoy the same customer recognition as more established offerings.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Our key initiatives include our recycling machine, the ‘ReclaMax’ shredder for Raffia waste and our pipeline includes the ‘ReclaPro’ cutter-compactor for film and post-consumer recycling, modular washing systems with wastewater treatment and AI-driven sorting technologies."
strategy_growth.title: RF 45: Limited experience in certain businesses proposed to be entered into

strategy_growth.detail: The Indian economy and its securities markets are influenced by economic developments and volatility in securities markets in other countries. Negative economic developments such as rising fiscal or trade deficits, or a default on national debt, in other emerging market countries, or an onset of recession, may affect investor confidence and cause increased volatility in Indian securities markets. The generalized system of preferences, a US trade preference program, is subject to changes and modification without notice, which could impact the duty structure applicable to certain products exported to the United States.
strategy_growth.evidence: "We cannot assure that our products will not be subject adverse duty levy in any of our export markets."
strategy_growth.title: RF 60: Recent global economic conditions have been challenging and continue to affect the Indian market

concerns_observed: Related-party intensity is rising sharply: absolute sum of all related party transactions was ₹4,593.39 million in FY2025, i.e. 33.36% of revenue from operations, versus 17.76% (₹2,070.21 million) in FY2024 and 6.61% (₹1,220.23 million) in FY2023 (RF 23).

The three-year record is not a like-for-like series: FY2025 is Restated Consolidated, FY2024 is a Restated Standalone shell with nil revenue and PAT of ₹(0.09) million, and FY2024/FY2023 comparatives are voluntary Special Purpose Combined and Carve-Out statements of the Demerged Business; the DRHP itself states neither set "should be used to forecast or accurately predict our future performance with any degree of certainty" (RF 46).

Revenue is concentrated in one machine family: woven Raffia machines were 87.28% of FY2025 revenue from operations (₹12,017.05 million), with circular looms at 31.54% and tape extrusion lines at 17.05% of the product split.

Order book has not grown across the period: ₹8,284.57 million as of March 31, 2025 against ₹7,692.40 million (March 31, 2024) and ₹8,747.62 million (March 31, 2023); the DRHP states order book information is not audited and may not be actualised (RF 17).

Demand history is volatile: carve-out revenue fell from ₹18,470.09 million in FY2023 to ₹11,658.08 million in FY2024 on fewer units produced, change in product mix and decline in sales to Africa, Asia Pacific (ex-India and China), Europe and MENA, before the FY2025 consolidated ₹13,768.72 million (RF 18).

Control remains concentrated after the Offer: Promoters and certain Promoter Group members held 93.00% of the issued and paid-up Equity Share capital as of the DRHP date, with Raj Kumar Lohia alone at 55.47%; the post-Offer promoter percentage is not populated in this draft (RF 51).

data_gaps: No like-for-like three-year series exists. Offer size in rupees, Price Band, P/E, market capitalisation to revenue and the post-Offer promoter percentage are all placeholders in this draft.

Promoter average cost of acquisition is disclosed (Raj Kumar Lohia ₹0.03, Gaurav Lohia ₹0.05, Amit Kumar Lohia ₹0.05 per share) but no reference or offer price is stated, so the cost-to-offer markup cannot be computed.

Balance sheet extraction is incomplete: total debt is not stated for any year in the restated balance-sheet extract (total borrowings of ₹1,851.74 million as of June 30, 2025 appear only in RF 16), and net fixed assets, CWIP, inventory and networth are absent for the carve-out years, so leverage and asset intensity cannot be traced across the period.

Capacity utilisation percentages are null for every product in every year; installed capacity for tape extrusion lines (240) and FIBC (8,000 tonnes) is given for FY2025 only, and RF 12 states installed capacity is interchangeable across products at a plant and rests on management estimates verified by a chartered engineer.

The litigation summary is largely unquantified: counts and amounts by party are null, with the aggregates (₹38.84 million by the Company, ₹17.29 million against the Company, ₹1.34 million against Directors) recoverable only from RF 37 evidence; total contingent liability is not aggregated into a single figure.

All eleven listed group companies carry null revenue, PAT and business description; only Lohia E-Mobility GmbH has a health note (insolvency proceedings expected to complete in 2027), so group financial health cannot be assessed.
Board committee composition is not captured (board size 8, 4 independent, committees list empty), the KMP list is empty, and ages are disclosed for only three of nine directors.

The KMP attrition table clusters almost every exit on April 30, May 6 and May 10, 2024, around the Scheme's May 1, 2024 effective date, and several named leavers (Gaurav Lohia, Rajendra Kumar Arya, P.K Mukherjee, Shikha Srivastava, Basant Seth, Naresh Kumar Gupta, Keith Reddy Padmaja Reddy) appear as current Directors or officers of the Company. verdict.our_read: Woven-Raffia machinery maker with 40.7% domestic and 15.4% global share by value and FY2025 revenue of ₹13,768.72 million at 31.71% ROE, whose thesis rides on whether the FY2025 consolidated base is repeatable against carve-out FY2023 revenue of ₹18,470.09 million.

parameter_scores.basis: 40.7% share by value of the domestic woven Raffia machines market in Fiscal 2025 and 15.4% of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value in 2024; installed base of over 2,300 tape extrusion lines, 468,000 winders and 96,000 circular looms as of March 31, 2025.

Three non-comparable bases across the disclosed period: FY2025 Restated Consolidated; FY2024 Restated Standalone with nil revenue and PAT of ₹(0.09) million; FY2024 and FY2023 Special Purpose Combined and Carve-Out statements of the Demerged Business, which the DRHP says involve estimates, assumptions and allocations and are not of the Company as it stands today (RF 46).

ROE 31.71%, ROCE 30.45%, EBITDA ₹2,286.02 million and PAT margin 8.5% on the Restated Consolidated FY2025 basis, against carve-out ROE of 11.92% (FY2024) and 23.66% (FY2023) and PAT margins of 2.54% and 3.06%.

Carve-out revenue ₹18,470.09 million (FY2023) to ₹11,658.08 million (FY2024), then ₹13,768.72 million on the FY2025 consolidated basis; order book ₹8,284.57 million at March 31, 2025 versus ₹8,747.62 million at March 31, 2023, and stated to be unaudited.

Net debt to equity 0.47x at March 31, 2025 versus 1.06x and 1.24x in the two prior years; total borrowings ₹1,851.74 million as of June 30, 2025; CRISIL AA-/Stable (cash credit, term loan) and CRISIL A1+ (forex forward, LC and BG, loan equivalent risk); no covenant default in the last three Fiscals per RF 16.

FY2025 Restated Consolidated CFO of ₹1,412.84 million against PAT of ₹1,178.41 million, with CFI ₹(312.93) million and CFF ₹(877.68) million; carve-out CFO was ₹1,115.14 million in FY2024 and an outflow of ₹(167.87) million in FY2023 (RF 6).

Woven Raffia machines were 87.28% of FY2025 revenue from operations; circular looms 31.54%, other machines and equipment 20.54% and tape extrusion lines 17.05% of the product split; exports 58.18% of revenue with top five export jurisdictions Egypt 4.39%, Iraq 4.21%, USA 3.99%, Sri Lanka 2.82% and Indonesia 2.58%.

Absolute related party transactions were 33.36% of FY2025 revenue from operations (₹4,593.39 million) versus 17.76% and 6.61% in the two prior years; recurring counterparties include United Trade.Net India (₹777.9 lakhs purchases FY2024), Vivsun Engineering (₹367.2 lakhs FY2024) and Sarjna Capfin, from which borrowings of ₹2,474.0 lakhs were taken in FY2024; corporate guarantee of ₹413.00 million for Leesona Corp.

Promoters and certain Promoter Group members hold 93.00% pre-Offer with Raj Kumar Lohia at 55.47%; board of 8 with 4 Independent Directors; show cause notice to Independent Director Dinesh Kumar Mittal under the SCRA, SEBI Act and SEBI Listing Regulations; auditor other matter on internal financial controls of two Indian subsidiaries; Promoters Raj Kumar Lohia and Gaurav Lohia may be entitled to a mutually agreed share of profits on non-machine commercialisation of assigned inventions (RF 53).

234 on-roll R&D employees (13.48% of on-roll manpower as at May 31, 2025) and R&D expenditure of ₹371.13 million (2.70% of FY2025 revenue, against 3.16% and 1.55% in the prior two years); 60 patents granted in India, 28 applied for, 56 granted globally; DSIR-accredited Hargovind Bajaj R&D Centre and NABL-accredited TTRC.

The Offer is entirely an Offer for Sale of up to 42,259,970 Equity Shares of face value ₹1 each and the Company will not receive any proceeds; there is no fresh issue. Offer size, Price Band, P/E and market-cap-to-revenue multiples are shown as placeholders, post-Offer promoter holding and dilution are not quantified, and the promoters' contribution and lock-in table is marked "To be updated in the Prospectus". The only valuation reference disclosed is the peer P/E band of 29.32 to 165.66 with an industry composite of 81.01.

Contingent items as of March 31, 2025: claims not acknowledged as debts ₹46.62 million, GST ₹17.12 million (penalty confirmed by order dated January 31, 2025, under appeal), income tax ₹0.17 million, capital commitments ₹54.23 million and corporate guarantees ₹413.00 million; litigation aggregates of ₹38.84 million by the Company, ₹17.29 million against the Company and ₹1.34 million against Directors; UPSIDA consent for the Offer unanswered and the Bengaluru facility building without an occupancy certificate.

A ₹413.00 million corporate guarantee to HSBC on behalf of subsidiary Leesona Corp, USA, which swung from a ₹38.26 million profit in FY2024 to a ₹102.12 million loss in FY2025; group company Lohia E-Mobility GmbH is in insolvency proceedings expected to complete in 2027.

The Promoter-majority Demerged Company, Lohia Trade Services Limited, remains authorised under its memorandum of association to manufacture technical textile machinery, and the family-settlement non-compete is time-limited to a 10-year Non-Compete Period.

The 'Lohia Group' brand under which the business operates is licensed from Lohia Trade Services Limited on a revocable, non-exclusive basis and may be terminated on a substantial change in the ownership of the Company.
A show cause notice has been issued to Independent Director Dinesh Kumar Mittal, including for violation of certain provisions of the SCRA, the SEBI Act and the SEBI Listing Regulations.

The owner of the building housing the Bengaluru manufacturing facility has not obtained an occupancy certificate as required by the local planning authority byelaws, which the DRHP states may compel relocation of that facility; UPSIDA consent for the Offer remains unanswered.
A ₹143.77 million write-down for slow and non-moving inventory was recorded in FY2025 against inventories of ₹2,962.12 million.
strengths_observed: Stated market share of 40.7% by value in the domestic woven Raffia machines market in Fiscal 2025 and 15.4% of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value in 2024 (RF 3, RF 8).
FY2025 Restated Consolidated return ratios of ROE 31.71%, ROCE 30.45% and PAT margin 8.5%, against Demerged-Business carve-out PAT margins of 2.54% (FY2024) and 3.06% (FY2023).

Net debt to equity fell to 0.47x as at March 31, 2025 from 1.06x (FY2024) and 1.24x (FY2023); total borrowings ₹1,851.74 million as of June 30, 2025; CRISIL AA-/Stable on cash credit and term loan and A1+ on short-term facilities.
FY2025 cash conversion: CFO of ₹1,412.84 million against PAT of ₹1,178.41 million, versus a carve-out CFO outflow of ₹(167.87) million in FY2023.
Export share of revenue rose from 35.81% (FY2023) to 49.50% (FY2024) to 58.18% (FY2025), led by MENA (10.03% to 16.62%) and North and South America (4.87% to 12.40%).

Installed base as of March 31, 2025 of over 2,300 tape extrusion lines, over 468,000 winders and 96,000 circular weaving looms, with spare parts contributing 12.62% of FY2025 revenue from operations (FY2024 11.95%, FY2023 8.19%).

In-house R&D of 234 on-roll employees (13.48% of on-roll manpower as at May 31, 2025) and spend of ₹371.13 million (2.70% of FY2025 revenue); 60 patents granted in India, 56 granted globally, 8 registered designs, 53 registered trademarks.

Backward integration into inverters, customised machine controllers and motors, an in-house surface-mount-technology PCB assembly line, sheet-metal fabrication, 100 CNC machines and in-house plating, moulding, assembly, testing and paint shops.
Permanent-employee attrition improved to 11.39% in FY2025 from 22.83% in FY2024 (12.94% in FY2023); 1,736 permanent employees as of May 31, 2025.
